queue.title: F295 change, section 2 -- shutdown ordering in the lifespan teardown
queue.detail: Done iteration 3. Tasks 2.1, 2.2, 2.3 built in hub/hub/main.py: _settle_background_runs() (+45 lines above lifespan) plus two calls appended to the teardown, after terminate_all_active_runs() and shutdown_scheduler(). Cancel, gather(return_exceptions=True), difference_update (not clear()), loop to a fixed point, bound at _MAX_BACKGROUND_SETTLE_PASSES = 5, WARNING with the leftover count on the bound rather than raising, then await engine.dispose(). The abandoned leftovers ARE cleared on the bound and the comment says why: the set is module-level, so a later lifespan in the same process would await tasks on a closed loop. DRIVEN in-process against the real lifespan() context manager (testbed/scratch/f295/probe_shutdown.py, uncommitted): A -- a pending run task is cancelled and settled and engine.pool is a different object after, so the dispose happened and happened after the settle; B -- a task re-registering a successor from its except CancelledError produces 6 tasks, exhausts the 5 passes, logs the WARNING and RETURNS rather than raising; C -- a dead-worker connection idle in the pool does not hang the teardown, 0.00s, neutralised. One finding for 3.6 to use: cancelling a task that has never run skips its except clause, so a test needs an await asyncio.sleep(0) before shutdown or the successor never spawns. 154 passed across every test file that boots the app plus test_agent_trigger and test_scheduler; ruff and black clean over CI's paths.

queue.title: F295 change, section 3 part A -- tests for the guard
queue.detail: Done iteration 4. Tasks 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.4, 3.7 built as hub/tests/test_dead_worker_connection.py -- five tests, 5 passed in 0.23s. The kill is 3.1's real mechanism transcribed into the file (second loop, future on it, close the loop, put on _tx, join, assert not is_alive); is_alive is never monkeypatched; every await is asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=15.0). A module autouse fixture disposes the engine BEFORE each test -- without it a connection pooled by an earlier test is handed out ahead of the victim and the test passes while asserting nothing. MUTATION-CHECKED, 4 of 4 product lines, engine restored and git diff confirmed empty after each: 1.2's raise -> return gives 3 named failures (46.20s); the checkout decorator removed gives those 3 plus the registration test (46.08s); the WARNING removed gives exactly 1 named failure (0.87s); 1.5's body -> return gives 1 named failure and then HANGS (killed at 180s, exit 124). That last row is a finding and is written into the module docstring: the hang is conftest's per-test dispose(), which no assertion in this file can bound, so a 1.5 regression costs a named failure followed by a stuck CI job -- and it is why 3.3 ships no listener-removed variant. 3.3's removal direction is confirmed twice instead: by that mutation, and by testbed/scratch/f295/probe_33_remove_close_checkout.py (uncommitted, event.remove under try/finally) -- keep RECOVERED in 0.00s, remove DID NOT RECOVER, timed out after 20.00s. queue.detail: Done iteration 5. FINDING, and the test docstring was corrected to match it: asyncio.wait_for does NOT bound engine.dispose() -- with 1.5 reverted, a 5s bound did not fire in 60s (probe_310_wait_for_bound.py, uncommitted), because the dispose reaches aiosqlite through SQLAlchemy's greenlet bridge. The same wait_for DOES bound the checkout/execute path.
